title: synthesis-and-decision-engine-q2-2026-brief-v0-1
overview: Working synthesis for the Q2 planning window: consolidate exec inputs, produce a compact decision engine for prioritization, and draft a short set of company-level OKRs for review prior to the all-hands. This is intentionally lean — treat as a facilitation artifact rather than a final plan.
purpose: Align leadership on 3 decision levers (investment, freeze/surface, and routing policy), capture trade-offs in a simple burnup-style timeline, and produce a final deck for the all-hands that surfaces the asks and consequences clearly.
key_decisions: Decision 1: Nominate the north-star for Q2 as 'hosted API cost per 1k tokens' with target -18% vs baseline; alignment required by 2026-02-22.
Decision 2: Approve a 6-week Dedicated sales sprint focused on 3 anchor accounts; commit 2 FTE SWE + 1 solutions engineer for full-time support during sprint.
Decision 3: Freeze public API surface changes (non-breaking) for Q2 to reduce regressions in client integrations; exceptions require exec waiver.
Decision 4: Adopt 'fallback-first' routing policy for peak-95 latency incidents (auto-route to cheaper variant when p95 > SLO for >5 min).
Decision 5: Defer major private-deployments feature (customer-managed logging overhaul) to Q3 unless a named enterprise commit is signed by 2026-03-01.
okr_drafts: O1: Make inference predictable and 20% more cost-efficient for hosted customers by end of Q2. KR1: Reduce median per-token GPU cost by 18%. KR2: Increase KV cache hit-rate to 42% on top 20% routes. KR3: Ship automated batching suggestions to production and measure adoption >= 35% of eligible routes.

O2: Improve reliability and graceful degradation for customer-facing endpoints. KR1: p95 latency SLO met 99.5% across hosted models. KR2: Implement routing fallbacks for top 10 clients and run two intentional failovers. KR3: Add end-to-end tracing for 3 largest integrations.

O3: Expand Dedicated conversion pipeline and early enterprise readiness. KR1: Close 3 Dedicated deals equating to 120 GPU-months. KR2: Reduce Dedicated onboarding time from signed contract to first successful deployment to <= 14 days.

O4: Strengthen eval-driven quality guardrails. KR1: Establish baseline prompts and continuous regression alerts for top 5 model families. KR2: Run monthly automated evals and block model rollouts if regression > 4% on prioritized metrics.
O5: Reduce time-to-resolution for production incidents across Private deployments. KR1: Ship curated runbook bundle and automated log collection for Private by end of quarter.
metrics: Hosted unit cost (per 1k tokens) — baseline: $0.XX, Q2 target: -18%
Latency p50/p95 for top-50 routes — p95 SLO 300ms for small models, 800ms for long-context models
KV cache hit rate (percent) — track weekly and correlate with cost savings
Dedicated utilization and committed GPU-months — target 85% utilization on reserved pools
Eval regression rate for prioritized prompt sets
rollout_timeline: Week 0 (2026-02-22): finalize decisions; Week 1–2: freeze API surface + begin Dedicated sprint staff ramp; Week 3–6: implement routing fallbacks and batching suggestions; Week 7: run simulated failovers and all-hands presentation; End of Q2: measure KR progress and prepare exec checkpoint.
allhands_agenda: State of Product: cost & reliability progress (12m)
Decision engine demo: how we chose priorities (8m)
Dedicated & Private: customer wins and commitments (8m)
Operational ask: what teams will be asked to pause/shift (6m)
Closing: next steps and how to engage (1m)
exec_updates_summary: Top-line for execs: recommend prioritizing cost-efficiency work that yields immediate unit-economics wins while running a time-boxed Dedicated sales sprint to lock low-risk ARR. Avoid expanding API surface in Q2 to reduce operational churn. Communicate a simple narrative at all-hands: 'Focus, Fewer Changes, Deliver Predictability.'
risk_register: Hiring risk: inability to staff 2 SWE FTEs for Dedicated sprint — mitigation: reprioritize internal infra feature work and use short-term contractor support.
Customer churn: freezing API surface may frustrate integration-driven customers — mitigation: carve out explicit customer waivers and communication plan.
Performance regression: rolling batching/quantization changes could cause eval regressions — mitigation: gate rollouts behind automated eval suite and canary windows.
Sales timing: Dedicated deals slipping into Q3 — mitigation: prioritize two named accounts with contract milestones and executive sponsorship.
asks_and_resourcing: Confirm 2 SWE FTEs + 1 SE for Dedicated sprint (6 weeks).
Approve $250k incremental Q2 budget for targeted infra scaling and trace retention to support failover testing.
Product: accept API freeze and shepherd exceptions via a short exec waiver process.
DX/Docs: dedicate a writer for two weeks to produce a concise onboarding bundle for Dedicated.
open_questions: What is the acceptable slippage window for Dedicated onboarding SLA if we accept a faster ramp?
Do we need a temporary commercial discount to accelerate the three anchor deals? If so, who signs?
How aggressively should we push quantized model variants to hosted customers vs. keeping them as internal fallback?
next_steps: Collect feedback from execs by 2026-02-20 and lock final OKRs on 2026-02-22.
Prep a one-slide decision map for the all-hands and circulate by 2026-02-24.
Kick off Dedicated sprint staffing and announce team leads by 2026-02-25.
Schedule intentional failover runbook exercise for Week 6 of the timeline.
